Simulate a reference set of hybrid histories

Source: R/reference.R
build_reference.Rd

Runs simulate_hybrid_zone() many times with settings drawn at random from the ranges given, and stacks every generation of every run. The ranges act as the prior of the estimator trained on the result, so they should cover what is plausible for the study system. The breeding population size matters most: past about five generations of a closed hybrid swarm, drift is the only clock left, and its speed depends on population size.

Usage

build_reference(
  n_sims = 4000,
  generations = 50,
  breeders = c(10, 500),
  start_mix = c(0.01, 0.99),
  arrival_max = 0.1,
  kinds = c(closed = 0.2, one = 0.4, both = 0.4),
  sib_mating = c(0, 0.9),
  pools = 4,
  n_markers = 1000,
  shared_freq = NULL,
  sample_size = 20,
  missing = 0,
  founders = "pure",
  map = NULL,
  map_scale = c(1, 1),
  assort = c(0, 0.8),
  het_dropout = c(0, 0.3),
  freq = NULL,
  microsat = NULL,
  founder_impurity = c(0, 0),
  founder_samples = FALSE,
  class_settings = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

n_sims

Number of simulated histories.

generations

Generations per history.

breeders

Range of breeding population sizes (drawn on a log scale). An effective size (Ne) range is usually the most relevant figure.

start_mix

Range of the founding share of species 2.

arrival_max

Largest share of breeders replaced by arrivals per generation.

kinds

Probabilities of closed, one-species and two-species arrival histories.

sib_mating

Range of sibling-mating probability; half the runs use 0.

pools

Largest number of breeding pools; half the runs use 1.

n_markers, shared_freq, sample_size, missing

Passed to simulate_hybrid_zone(). Match these to the observed data.

founders

Founding designs to draw from (see simulate_hybrid_zone()): "pure" for natural contact, or "F1", "BC1_1", "BC1_2" for experimental or hatchery populations.

map

Linkage: NULL for unlinked markers; a marker map (see random_map()) used by every history; or a list with ranges chromosomes and length_cM, from which each history draws its own random map, so that an unknown genome enters the reference as uncertainty. A fixed map should hold the observed markers' real positions, in the order of the diagnostic markers; then genotype switches along chromosomes are summarized too (see sample_summaries()).

map_scale

With a fixed map, a range by which positions are multiplied in each history, for an uncertain recombination rate (for example, positions in Mb with map_scale = c(0.5, 3) for 0.5-3 cM per Mb).

assort

Range of the probability of mating by ancestry (see simulate_hybrid_zone()); half the runs use 0.

het_dropout

Range of the probability that a heterozygote is called homozygous; half the runs use 0 unless the range excludes 0. Give c(0, 0) for genotyping methods without allele dropout.

freq

Optional allele frequencies for markers that are not fixed (see simulate_hybrid_zone()); observed scores must then come from hybrid_scores(method = "likelihood").

microsat

Optional microsatellite markers (see microsat_markers()); observed scores must then come from hybrid_scores_microsat(), and n_markers is set to the number of loci.

founder_impurity

Range of the share of diagnostic alleles that founders carry from the other species (see simulate_hybrid_zone()), drawn for each history.

founder_samples

With F1 or backcross founders, also include samples of the founders themselves (generation 0), for experimental families of F1s or first backcrosses (see simulate_hybrid_zone()).

class_settings

Settings of the classes behind the class shares in the summaries (see class_settings()): genotyping error, heterozygote dropout, linked markers, and reference allele frequencies for markers that are not fixed. They are stored with the reference and used again by estimate_history(), so that the data are classified the same way.

cores

Number of processes (forked; 1 on Windows).

seed

Base random seed; run i uses seed + i.

Value

A data.frame of all generations of all runs, with the run's settings (run, breeders, start_mix, arrival1, arrival2 and their timing1, timing2 and switch1, switch2 generations, kind, sib_mating, pools), the true history and the summaries. Attribute settings records the arguments.

Details

Each run is one of three kinds of history, with probabilities kinds: a closed swarm (no arrivals after founding), arrivals of one species only (repeated backcrossing), or arrivals of both species (ongoing hybridization). Arrivals of each species are, with equal probability, constant, stop at a random generation, or start at a random generation, so that the reference includes hybridization that has ended and hybridization that began late.

Examples

# \donttest{
ref <- build_reference(n_sims = 20, generations = 10, n_markers = 200)
dim(ref)
#> [1] 200 127
# }
